installation.title: Installation
installation.description: Add Solaris UI to a new or existing Angular project in minutes: install the package, wire styles and providers, and render your first component.

ai.prompt: I'm looking at the Solaris UI documentation for {{component}} ({{url}}). Help me understand how to use it. Be ready to explain concepts, give examples, or help debug based on it.

prerequisites.note: Solaris targets standalone Angular applications. You need Node.js LTS and one package manager.
prerequisites.angular: Angular 21 or later with a standalone bootstrap (ApplicationConfig).
prerequisites.node: Node.js LTS with pnpm, npm, yarn, or bun.
prerequisites.peers: Peer dependencies (such as @angular/cdk) install automatically with the package.

install.note: Install the single package, then let the schematic wire the rest.
install.schematic: Recommended: run ng add. It creates src/styles/solaris.scss, imports it from your global stylesheet, and adds provideSolaris(...) to the app config.
install.nx: On Nx workspaces, install the package and run the init generator instead of ng add.
install.manual: Prefer to wire things yourself? Skip the schematic and follow the styles and providers sections below.

styles.note: The schematic creates this stylesheet and imports it from your global styles. Manual setups copy both blocks.
styles.global: Prepended to your global stylesheet (for example src/styles.scss).

providers.note: Register Solaris services once in the app config. Start minimal; add theme or translation options only when you need them.

language.note: Translation is opt-in: without it, providers fall back to defaults. When you need it, pass the locale, a fallback locale, and your flattened translation maps.

verify.note: Start the dev server and open the app. Theme tokens and base styles apply globally — no component import is needed for the foundation.
verify.success: If the page renders with the Solaris look and feel, the setup is complete. Continue with the icon library or any component page.
